definitions.explanation: A person who travels from place to place selling goods, rather than operating from a fixed shop. Historically common in Japan before the modern retail era.

examples.japanese: {行商人|ぎょうしょうにん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{村|むら}→村：02261_mura⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦やって→やる：02980_yaru⟧きた。
examples.english: A peddler came to the village.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{行商人|ぎょうしょうにん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{行|い}き{来|き}していた→行き来する：22992_ikikisuru⟧。
examples.english: In the old days, peddlers used to come and go along this road.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{若|わか}い⟦ころ→〜ころ：03091_koro⟧{行商人|ぎょうしょうにん}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{全国|ぜんこく}→全国：03311_zenkoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{回|まわ}り→回る：01150_mawaru⟧、⟦{魚|さかな}→魚：00499_sakana⟧や⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{売|う}り{歩|ある}いて⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: When my grandfather was young, he traveled the country as a peddler, selling fish and vegetables.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{行商|ぎょうしょう}→行商：20193_gyoushou⟧ (peddling, itinerant trade) and ⟦{人|にん}→〜人：00658_nin⟧ (person). The base word ⟦{行商|ぎょうしょう}→行商：20193_gyoushou⟧ can also be used on its own to refer to the activity of peddling.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{行商|ぎょうしょう}→行商：20193_gyoushou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to peddle)
- ⟦{行商|ぎょうしょう}→行商：20193_gyoushou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧ (to go out peddling)
- {行商人|ぎょうしょうにん}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧ (to work as a peddler)

Historically, {行商人|ぎょうしょうにん} played an important role in distributing goods to rural areas. Today the term appears mainly in historical contexts. Modern equivalents include {移動販売|いどうはんばい} (mobile sales) for food trucks and similar businesses.
